questions.stem: When calculating enthalpy change per mole from calorimetry data, after finding Q using Q = mcΔT, what is the next step?

options.text: Multiply Q by the number of moles
Multiply Q by the specific heat capacity
Divide Q by the mass of water used
Divide Q by the number of moles of reactant and add the correct sign

questions.explanation: After calculating Q (energy transferred in joules), you convert to kJ by dividing by 1000, then divide by the number of moles of the reactant to get kJ/mol. If the temperature increased, ΔH is negative (exothermic); if it decreased, ΔH is positive (endothermic).
